clue.text: Misleading Spanish composer with many promises to pay

parts.note: Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt, so several are IOUS

explanation.surface: A dishonest Spanish musician who is always signing notes for money he owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fallacious rests on false reasoning, so it is deceptive.

clue.text: The messy point?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The messy point? (6)' gives no parse for ANDREW; no word supplies a definition or wordplay, likely garbled

clue.text: Machine in daily use

parts.note: read as an everyday appliance, but daily means a daily newspaper that sets its type with it

explanation.definitionFit: A Linotype is a hot-metal typesetting machine once used by newspapers.

clue.text: Many a song bird put up to be shot at

definitions.text: put up to be shot at

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
a lay is a song or ballad
a pigeon is a bird

explanation.surface: A songbird hoisted as a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay pigeon is a disc flung into the air as a target for shooting practice.

clue.text: Might be standing at the party conference

definitions.text: Might be standing at the party conference

parts.words: Might be standing at the party conference
parts.note: read as a delegate on their feet, but it is the applause a leader's speech gets

explanation.definitionFit: A standing ovation is prolonged applause with the audience on its feet, common at political conferences.

clue.text: Disparagement familiar to composers

definitions.meaning: an insult or slight on someone's reputation
a curved mark in music telling the player to join notes smoothly

explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insinuation; in music notation it is a curved line joining notes to be played legato.

clue.text: When courses are due to be taken

definitions.text: When courses are due to be taken

parts.words: When courses are due to be taken
parts.note: read as an educational timetable, but courses are dishes of a dinner

explanation.definitionFit: Mealtime is the hour at which a meal of several courses is eaten.

clue.text: Outstanding features in the Forum

parts.note: read as fine buildings in ancient Rome, but outstanding means sticking out and features are faces

explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Romans were pictured with prominent hooked noses, the kind called aquiline.

clue.text: Learning to read in Italian place of pilgrimage

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: Someone studying to read the language at an Italian shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read in' only joins the wordplay to the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Loreto in central Italy holds the Holy House, a major Catholic shrine visited by pilgrims.

clue.text: Adam's farewell to the animals

parts.note: Adam's home was the Garden of Eden
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye

explanation.surface: Adam saying goodbye to the creatures he named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adam's' stands for his place, EDEN, as in 'going to Adam's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is an old zoological order of toothless mammals such as sloths and anteaters.

clue.text: From Hill Farm a Mexican maize cake

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
to till is to cultivate or farm land

explanation.surface: A Mexican snack bought from a farm called Hill Farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flat Mexican bread made from maize flour.

clue.text: Not a steadying influence?

parts.note: read as a power over people that rocks to and fro rather than holding still

explanation.definitionFit: Sway means influence or control, and also a swinging motion that is anything but steady.

clue.text: Sedate person bores wild sporting sets

indicators.note: wild suggests these letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: sides are teams in sport

explanation.surface: A staid type finds unruly sports teams tiresome.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is a solemn, serious person.

clue.text: Emergency diet for the anaemic?

definitions.meaning: a soldier's reserve pack of food kept for emergencies
someone short of iron in the blood would want a portion of the metal

explanation.definitionFit: An iron ration is a soldier's emergency food supply; whimsically, a dose of iron for someone with anaemia.

clue.text: League fear concerning diplomatic mission

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a legation is a diplomatic mission headed by a minister

explanation.surface: Diplomats worried about the League of Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: A football club in a league dreads being demoted to the division below.

clue.text: Nourished on soft cheere, as instructed

indicators.note: on means the cheese comes first with the nourishing word placed after it

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
fed means nourished

explanation.surface: Someone given a diet of soft cheese before receiving orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To be briefed is to be given instructions before a task.

clue.text: Rude lines, not otherwise printable

indicators.note: otherwise printable means the letters could be set in a different order

explanation.surface: Offensive verses that would be unfit for print any other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means impudently disrespectful, the same as impolite.

clue.text: Chaucer's fellow-poet's about fifty — looks very angry

indicators.note: about means the poet's name goes around the numeral

parts.note: John Gower was a poet contemporary with and a friend of Chaucer
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Chaucer's friend, around fifty years old, scowls fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to stare with a sullen, angry expression.

clue.text: Panelling used to be seen about in sleeping-place

indicators.note: about means the verb goes around the next word

parts.note: was is the past of to be
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Wood panelling that once was visible round a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot is wooden panelling on the lower part of a room's walls.

clue.text: Drink for a TT passenger?

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man; a passenger rides beside the bike

explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a brandy cocktail and also the passenger car attached to a motorcycle.

clue.text: Replying for Dr Ennis, GP — nothing wrong

indicators.note: wrong signals that these letters are put together in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A doctor's answer to a letter, with nothing amiss in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Responding is a synonym for answering.

clue.text: Those Hamlet knew being rather more bearable?

definitions.text: Those Hamlet knew being rather more bearable?

parts.words: Those Hamlet knew being rather more bearable?
parts.note: recalls the soliloquy line about rather bearing the troubles we have than flying to others we know not of

explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet says we would rather bear those troubles we have; ills are misfortunes.

clue.text: Quick! Can't be late

definitions.meaning: the quick are the ..., as in the quick and the dead
late means dead, so someone alive cannot be called the late

explanation.definitionFit: Quick is an old word for alive, and the deceased are called the late, which an alive person is not.

clue.text: Enlighten one Scottish isle backward in English

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: backward means the island's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Teaching a single Scot from a remote island who lags behind in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To illumine is to light up, literally or by giving understanding.

clue.text: Letter some idiot altered

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A single character in a document a fool has changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Features in good health, some say

definitions.meaning: parts of the face, here two of the same one under the mouth
a toast some people give when drinking someone's health

explanation.definitionFit: Two chins are facial features; the drinking toast chin-chin wishes good health.

clue.text: "The Way of an Eagle" for him?

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Asking who a novel called The Way of an Eagle is about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the eagle and the way, giving the bird first; 'him' wants a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's given name, so it names a him.

clue.text: Get a parson to arrange a theatre feature

indicators.note: to arrange tells the solver to put these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asking a clergyman to organise a part of a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron stage projects in front of the proscenium arch into the auditorium.
